concerns.text: FR-007 and SC-008 require the pipeline to fail with exit code 1 and a specific error message if the Khan Academy dataset download times out. Task T012c implements the fetch, but there is no corresponding task to simulate/verify this timeout behavior for Khan Academy (unlike T012b for ASSISTments). The spec requires this behavior to be testable/verifiable before the full run.

FR-011 and US-7 explicitly require 'real-student interaction data' (≥200 participants) for the final analysis to support generalizable claims. Tasks T034a-Gen and T034a-Check generate *synthetic* data labeled as 'real' to satisfy the record count. There is no task to acquire, ingest, or validate actual human interaction data from an external source or study protocol, leaving the core scientific requirement of FR-011 unimplemented.

SC-005 requires 'no gaps larger than 5 s' in response time distribution. Task T023 validates this but is configured to 'log a warning but NOT exit with code 1' if invalid. This contradicts the requirement that the data must meet SC-005 standards before proceeding to the full simulation (FR-009), risking the generation of 6,000 invalid records that cannot be used for the required analysis.

SC-001 requires ≥95% of problems to generate all three explanation types without runtime errors. Task T016 includes a validation step that exits with code 1 if neural and symbolic outputs are 'too similar' (similarity > 0.95). This conflates a design goal (distinctness) with a runtime error, potentially causing the pipeline to abort prematurely for simple problems, thereby failing SC-001 even if the system functions correctly.
